capabilities: Branch LLM conversations as node graphs with input and generate cards
Attach files (.md, .canvas, .docx, .fountain) and web pages as prompt inputs
Call LLM providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, or local runtimes
Simulate user-model and model-model dialogues with per-model system prompts
Connect MCP-compatible servers to give models external tools and data
disambiguation: Not the Canvas learning-management system; it is a node-based canvas UI for talking with LLMs inside Obsidian.
extras: MCP support is marked experimental and requires editing data.json with Claude Desktop-compatible configs. Some providers (Google, OpenRouter, SambaNova) offer free models, so API keys are not always needed.
intentEvidence: Let me introduce an alternative: a canvas-like UI.
problem: Linear chat interfaces become inefficient and overwhelming when exploring multiple prompt branches in complex research work.

relations.evidence: Canvas LLM is powered by Svelte Flow from xyflow.

requires.name: Local LLM runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp)

summary: Canvas-style node editor for chatting with LLMs, using branching conversations built from input, generate, and dialogue cards.
